item.title: Kinkazan Island: Sacred Deer & Monkeys — Guide
item.description: Kinkazan — ‘Gold Flower Mountain’ — is one of Japan’s three great power spots, a sacred island off the Oshika Peninsula where hundreds of sika deer and wild macaque monkeys roam freely among the ancient shrine buildings. Koganeyama Shrine at the island’s centre has been a pilgrimage destination since the 8th century, and traditional belief holds that three consecutive January visits guarantee lifelong financial fortune. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Ishinomaki (Oshika Peninsula), Miyagi Hours Ferry ~9:00–15:00 (seasonal) Admission Around ¥1,000 (island entry) Time needed About 2 hours Best time Year-round; January for the pilgrimage tradition What to See Hundreds of free-roaming sika deer and wild macaques.
